data.statement: Map malformed cleanup.json quality metrics to CleanupDocumentError so project validation returns repair-required evidence instead of leaking TypeError

acceptance: Loading a completed cleanup.json whose introduced_fusion_count is null raises CleanupDocumentError and never leaks TypeError.

Each required blocking quality metric is present as a non-boolean integer; malformed or missing values and nonzero values are rejected as CleanupDocumentError, while zero-valued valid metrics remain accepted.

Progress fields required by the Cleanup V2 contract and by resume/manifest projection are validated for required keys and safe shapes so missing or malformed progress data raises CleanupDocumentError rather than a downstream KeyError, TypeError, or AttributeError.

Opening a project whose manifest claims completed Cleanup but whose cleanup.json contains a malformed blocking quality metric returns repair_required for the Cleanup step instead of propagating an exception.
Existing valid Cleanup loading, completion evidence, resume, manual-edit, and project-repair behavior remains unchanged.
Focused tests, the complete pytest and Ruff gates, and traceability/coverage audits pass without blocking findings.
assumptions: project_workspace_service's existing OSError/ValueError completion-evidence boundary is the intended consumer contract; the fix belongs in text_cleanup_service rather than a broader consumer catch.
data.reason: The defect is confined to one strict document boundary, the exception contract is already established, the project consumer already handles CleanupDocumentError through ValueError, and focused direct plus end-to-end regressions bound the change.
scope: In scope: strict validation of the Cleanup progress structure and completed-document blocking quality metrics; normalization of malformed loaded data to CleanupDocumentError; focused loader and project-open repair regressions; a durable requirement, Cleanup V2 specification detail, and Text Cleanup/Project Lifecycle documentation review. Out of scope: Cleanup metric generation, renderer semantics, non-Cleanup artifacts, UI changes, broad TypeError catches in project_workspace_service, schema migration/versioning, chunking behavior, and unrelated validation hardening.
data.source: Gitea issue #33: http://192.168.1.15:3001/dpasare/2026_AudioMancer/issues/33; remediation order in issue #40
data.understanding: The strict Cleanup document validator currently coerces four blocking quality metrics with int(), allowing malformed JSON values such as null to leak TypeError instead of the documented CleanupDocumentError. Because project completion evidence intentionally catches OSError and ValueError, that leak crashes project opening instead of treating Cleanup as invalid and offering the normal repair path. Harden the validator at the document boundary, including the progress fields consumed by resume and manifest projection, while preserving the existing valid Cleanup schema and project-workspace exception policy.
